chunks: As-Sayyid ar-Raḍī says: Verses have also been related from Amīr al-mu’minīn on the same matter, which are:

If you claim to have secured authority by consultation, how did it happen when those to be consulted were absent! If you have scored over your opponents by kinship then someone else has greater right for being nearer to the Holy Prophet.
ai.seo_question: What is the Shia critique of political legitimacy based on consultation and kinship?
ai.summary: As-Sayyid ar-Raḍī cites this verse to highlight the theological tension between the Sunni concept of *shura* (consultation) and the Shia emphasis on *nass* (divine designation) through the Prophet's kin. The poem argues that if political legitimacy rests on the consensus of companions, their absence renders the system unstable; conversely, if it rests on lineage, the Ahl al-Bayt possess a superior, inherent claim to authority as the closest relatives of the Prophet.
